title: Perfect Modals
summary: Modal + have + past participle expresses past deduction, regret, criticism, or missed possibility.

theory.markdown:
**Perfect modals** = **modal + have + past participle**

They refer to **past** situations that are now over.

**should have done** — criticism or regret (you didn't, but it would have been better)
*You should have told me earlier.* (you didn't — I'm criticising)
*I shouldn't have eaten so much.* (I regret it)

**must have done** — past deduction (near-certain it happened)
*She must have left — her coat is gone.*

**can't have done** — past deduction (near-certain it didn't happen)
*He can't have stolen it — he wasn't even there.*

**might / could have done** — past possibility (it was possible but uncertain)
*They might have missed the train.* / *I could have made a mistake.*

**would have done** — hypothetical past result (in conditionals)
*I would have helped if you had asked.*

**needn't have done** — something was done but was unnecessary
*You needn't have worried — everything was fine.*

theory.title: Perfect modals at a glance
rows: I shouldn't have been so rude.
You needn't have cooked so much.

items.source: You shouldn't have spent so much money on that.
items.translation: Nie powinieneś/powinnaś był/a wydawać tyle pieniędzy na to.

items.source: She must have worked very hard to achieve all this.
items.translation: Musiała bardzo ciężko pracować, żeby to wszystko osiągnąć.

items.source: I could have done better on the exam if I'd slept more.
items.translation: Mógłbym/Mogłabym lepiej napisać egzamin, gdybym więcej spał/a.

exercises.prompt: You ___ told me about the party! I didn't know.
exercises.explanation: 'Should have' = criticism — you didn't tell me, but you should have.

exercises.prompt: She looks terrible. She ___ (must / sleep) badly last night.
exercises.hint: Past deduction (near-certain): must have + past participle.

answers: I should not have said that.

exercises.prompt: I ___ (needn't / buy) so much food — half of it went to waste.
exercises.hint: The buying was unnecessary → needn't have + past participle.

exercises.sentence: He could has finished earlier if he had focused.
answers: He could have finished earlier if he had focused.
exercises.explanation: Perfect modal: modal + HAVE + past participle (not 'has').
